name: Spitify
subtitle: Your music, podcasts & audiobooks
description: Official source for Spitify, a Spotify-style player for the music on your phone.

apps.name: Spitify
apps.subtitle: Spotify-style player for your own music
apps.localizedDescription: Play the music, podcasts and audiobooks on your iPhone with playlists made for you, learned on the device. Synced lyrics, crossfade, a 10-band EQ, free LibriVox audiobooks, automatic artwork and tag fixing, and themes. No account, no ads.

privacy.NSAppleMusicUsageDescription: Spitify can play the songs already downloaded in your Music library.
privacy.NSCameraUsageDescription: Take a picture of a Spotify code to open its playlist, song, or other item.
privacy.NSPhotoLibraryUsageDescription: Choose a profile picture or custom artwork.
privacy.NSSiriUsageDescription: Use Siri to play music and control Spitify.

versions.localizedDescription:
Spitify 1.0.24 brings Spitify to your computer and frees up space taken by FLAC files.

- **Spitify Desktop:** the same app for macOS (Apple silicon and Intel), Windows and Linux. It plays your own music folders and streams, downloads, podcasts, audiobooks, lyrics, Made for you mixes, Friends and Listening Rooms. It has a wide layout with the player beside your library, keyboard shortcuts and media keys. Download the installer for your computer below. The installers aren't signed yet:
  - **Mac:** open Spitify once, then go to System Settings › Privacy & Security and click **Open Anyway**.
  - **Windows:** if SmartScreen warns you, choose **More info › Run anyway**.
- **Downloads are AAC:** new downloads are saved as AAC 256 kbps (.m4a) instead of FLAC, which is about a third of the size and sounds the same to most ears.
- **Convert existing FLAC:** **Settings › Convert FLAC to AAC** re-encodes the FLAC files already in your library and deletes the originals after you confirm. Likes, playlists, play counts and lyrics carry over. Nothing is converted unless you choose to.

The iPhone download is unsigned for SideStore/AltStore. The Android APK installs directly.

Spitify 1.0.23 makes downloads easy to find and fixes more of what made Android lag.

- **Downloads everywhere:** every song row now shows whether it plays offline. A green mark means it's on your phone; a download button means it's streamed. Tap the button to download, or the progress ring to cancel. Albums, playlists, mixes and All Songs have a **Download all** button that turns into a check once everything is offline. Search results can be downloaded too.
- **Less lag on Android:** streamed songs no longer rewrite a large settings file each time one starts. The download manager no longer checks every downloaded file each second while any download is pending or waiting to retry.
- **Lag reports:** if Android still feels slow, use it for a few minutes, then **Settings → Send problem report**. The report now shows where the app was stuck.
- **Music video and Canvas are off** while a better video source is chosen.

The iPhone download is unsigned for SideStore/AltStore. The Android APK installs directly.

Spitify 1.0.22 makes streaming smooth on Android, replaces music videos with Canvas, and fixes bugs on both phones.

- **Canvas:** the camera button beside the song title loops a few silent seconds of the song's official music video behind the player, in 1080p for most modern videos. Clips come from Apple's music-video previews, so they belong to the exact song; songs without a video show their artwork. Playback is native and cached, with no web view.
- **Smooth streaming on Android:** podcasts and streamed songs no longer make the app lag. Cover art is sized for the lock screen, autoplay works in the background instead of blocking the screen, and a hidden YouTube page no longer loads on every song.
- **Lighter player on both phones:** lyrics, the mini player and widgets only redraw when something visible changes. Streams show a spinner while buffering.
- **Delete any playlist:** imported and shared playlists can be deleted or removed, and generated mixes can be deleted (bring them back in Settings).
- **Fixes:** "Remove from this playlist" could remove the wrong song. Album-to-album navigation broke Back on Android. Plain-http podcasts were blocked on iPhone. Audiobooks with no chapters crashed. Android re-asked to edit audio files on every launch, and some podcast downloads crashed it.

The iPhone download is unsigned for SideStore/AltStore. The Android APK installs directly.

HD music videos, album download buttons in search, playlist artwork and deletion, clearer library actions, and artist lookup fixes. Keep app extensions when installing to retain the artwork and playback widgets.

Now Playing with cover art and playback controls, plus playlist, album, most-played, recent and liked-song widgets. Simpler Profile and Friends pages and sharper photos. Keep app extensions when installing through SideStore.
Friends profiles and picture codes, saved playlist repairs, artist covers and hiding, three widgets, OS backup support, better Shortcuts lookup, and new borders for all 25 themes.

25 new art themes for iPhone and Android, with custom pixel art, matching colours and quiet borders. Choose a look in Settings → Appearance → Art themes, or turn off the art while keeping its colours.

Add public Spotify playlists from Library → Add from Spotify. Preview the cover and songs before saving. Regular playlist links and Spotify short links are supported.

Scan Spotify picture codes from Search or the Library menu. Choose a photo or take a picture; the bars are read on your phone. Playlist codes open a playlist preview. Other supported items offer their Spotify link and a matching search in Spitify. Keep the bars clear, level and fully visible. Spotify lookup needs internet and uses an unofficial web-player service that can change.

The iPhone download is unsigned for SideStore/AltStore. The Android APK installs directly.

Spitify 1.0.17 brings the album page’s look across the app on iPhone and Android.

- Albums, imported and shared playlists, artists, podcasts and books now use shared headers, title spacing and action bars.
- Play uses the same round button. Save, download, share, queue and shuffle use matching icon controls where those actions apply.
- Songs, episodes and chapters follow shared row spacing and text styles. Playlists keep song artwork, albums keep track numbers, and books keep portrait covers.
- Page titles, back buttons, forms and sheets follow the chosen theme more consistently.
- The shared layouts account for longer titles, larger text and wider Android screens.
- Online artist song taps start the artist list from that song. Imported playlists and shared queues highlight the song currently playing.

Checked the main screens, light mode, large text, folded and unfolded Android layouts, and the actual playback, save, menu and back controls.

Install the APK on Android. The unsigned IPA can be signed with SideStore or AltStore. The SideStore source also includes this update.

Spitify 1.0.16 improves music videos, playlists, library artists and iPhone streaming.

- Videos now use up to ten longer passages spread through the recording. The last picture stays visible while the next passage loads, then fades into it. Pausing also holds an unfinished fade, and resuming or returning to the app restarts the moving picture. A discarded video frame no longer prevents later passages from playing.
- Playlists have a cover, clear Play/Shuffle/Save buttons, song artwork, full-row playback and song menus. Removed the “Open original playlist” link.
- Your Library lists main artists. Guest credits remain available from songs, without adding guest-only artists or giving them another artist's album cover.
- Album loading checks the returned release and rejects unrelated duplicate-numbered tracks. This removes the Tay-K entry supplied with Phoebe Bridgers' Punisher. The source is still missing ICU; the app does not fill its place with an unrelated song.
- Podcasts and audiobooks always show their covers. Returning to music restores the chosen artwork style.
- All 25 icon designs keep the same artwork, cropped closer to fill their space.
- iPhone streams retry a failed first start once before moving on. Repeated vinyl seeks finish in order and follow the latest finger position instead of repeatedly cancelling the audio decoder. Normal-speed playback also avoids the extra pitch processing that made the Buggles recording silent during a drag; changed playback speed

Volume normalization is on by default. Fix playback after output changes, read real audio formats, keep queues going, and keep download progress visible. Separate featured artists and make rows easier to tap. Improve layouts, text, buttons, contrast, search, and retry messages throughout the main screens. Add 12 themes, 25 vinyl app icons, realistic record artwork, and a saved artwork-style button. Videos use short muted loops, fill the screen, hide embedded controls, and hold their frame on pause. Keep prepared clips safe when songs change. Add more Siri shortcuts; full Siri music requests require a Siri-enabled signing profile. Physical Bluetooth switching and spoken Siri still need a device check.

Full-height centered video behind controls, remembered video mode, and immediate prepared video display. Fix Home navigation, full playlist-row taps, and unnamed duplicate albums. Reduce Android work during streaming. Save both Android wallpapers before showing album art, keep backups after failed restoration, and turn the feature off if the phone changes Home too. Older missing wallpaper backups cannot be recovered.

Music videos now fill the screen, including behind the status bar. Song controls stay hidden in video mode; tap the video to return to the player. This also applies to Android's foldable layouts.

Video matching accepts label uploads, alternate title formatting, reuploads, and longer music-video edits. If a video cannot play, the player tries another match. Lookup starts when a song starts. Recent matches stay in memory for up to a day (100 songs maximum), and one embedded player stays ready for reuse. Artwork stays visible until video playback starts, without a fetching message. This does not download videos for offline use.

Captions are requested off when the player loads and when caption modules arrive. Text burned into the video cannot be removed. YouTube can still display its own branding or ads.

All Songs now has sorting by Title, Artist, Album, Recently Added, and Most Played. The audio output at the bottom uses the accent colour and opens the phone's device picker; older Android versions use the system audio settings.

Checks: 59 iPhone unit tests passed, six optional tests skipped; six Android device tests passed. Both release builds and the shared video-control checks passed. Physical-phone appearance and audio-device switching still need a device check. The earlier GitHub-hosted lock-screen-artwork test failure has not been claimed fixed.

Downloads now retry short outages and try another matching source when the first source fails. Failed downloads from the previous release can recover when the app opens. Songs keep their titles, album details, and cover art inside the saved files.

Search opens a full song or album page. Saved songs can play right away. Missing songs stay grey with a small download circle, and become playable when saved. Album downloads sit beside the play controls. Search no longer shows storage folders. Profile controls stay below the notch, and both apps include a Wi-Fi-only download setting.

Checked real backup downloads for all 28 songs on The Beatles’ Love on iOS, repeated checks for three affected songs, and real playback of three backup downloads on Android. Also checked Android recovering from a real first-source failure through the normal album page. Source availability can still vary by song and over time.

Checks: iOS and Android release builds succeeded. Android's 34 unit tests passed. iOS ran 36 unit tests with three opt-in network tests skipped, plus three passing page-layout tests. The separate live download tests passed. Android's wider lint check still reports 36 errors in unchanged playback and UI files.

Spitify 1.0.9 brings the combined music search and the latest player fixes to Android and iPhone.

- Search local and online songs together, ranked by the same match rules. Switch between Songs and Albums. Explicitly unavailable songs stay out of search results.
- All Songs replaces Liked Songs. Use the library and playlists to keep music.
- Hide or restore recommendations in Settings. Open Settings from the Home menu; find listening stats in Profile.
- Keep guest tracks together in their album without losing the individual artist credits.
- Turn the vinyl record to move within the current song. Fix the Android swipe that could leave the player half open.
- Keep the player's background continuous through the status bar, give top controls room, and request higher refresh rates on supported screens.
- Make album downloads an icon with clear feedback. Improve cover-image retries and save the checked cover from the preview.
- Add on-device alternate-audio attempts when a primary download fails. Matching AAC audio stays labelled AAC; blocked or unavailable recordings still fail honestly.
- Add lock-screen artwork controls. A short pause keeps the art. Stop, close, or 10 minutes idle ends it where the OS lets the app run.

**Lock-screen setup and limits:** Android needs Settings → Allow wallpaper backup → All files access to save and restore a still wallpaper. Live wallpapers stay unchanged. A forced process kill may defer restoration until the next launch. iOS 26+ gets a local

- Songs you add to the queue now play before the rest of the album or library, in the order you added them. Your picks are shown separately.
- Missing song details and covers are filled automatically and saved into local music files. Existing tags and artwork are kept. Android may ask for permission to update files added by another app.
- New downloads include their song details and cover art in the file. Manual edits also save into the file.
- Pages stop above the bottom player. Discover Weekly and Release Radar have been removed.
- Added Siri shortcuts and Android voice-search handling for music, playlists, podcasts, and books. Try “Play [name] in Spitify” on Siri. Real Siri/Gemini recognition still needs a phone check.
- Added iPhone CarPlay browsing screens. The separate Spitify icon requires an Apple-approved CarPlay signing profile; the normal SideStore build keeps that restricted permission off. The car's built-in Now Playing screen uses Spitify's existing playback controls.

The combined local/online search and All Songs library entry are planned for the next release.

Checks: 24 Android unit tests, three Android device tests, 22 iPhone unit tests, and an iPhone player-spacing check passed. The optional live download test was skipped.

Install the APK on Android or the unsigned IPA through SideStore on iPhone. The mapping text file is only for decoding Android crash reports.

- Swipe a song right to add it to the queue, with haptic feedback and a brief confirmation.
- Queue buttons now confirm how many songs were added. Unsupported files and a player that is still connecting get a clear message.
- The player shows the current audio output, such as Phone speaker or the headphone name reported by your phone.
- Opening a podcast search result no longer follows it. Tap Follow when you want to add it to Your shows.
- Unfollowing a podcast keeps its cached episode details and downloads.
- Keep scrolling artist and album artwork inside its frame, fixing the exposed strip below the artist photo.

Includes the Monochrome music downloads and Android icon change from 1.0.6.

Android release build and unit tests passed. iPhone unit tests passed, including a check of podcast follow/unfollow behaviour. Physical-phone gestures, haptics and Bluetooth route names still need a device check.

The Android APK is attached. GitHub builds and attaches the iPhone IPA after publication, then updates SideStore.

The mapping text file is for decoding Android crash reports; you do not need it to install the app.

- Search for songs and albums under Search → Online on Android and iPhone.
- Download music from Monochrome into your library for offline playback.
- Downloads use Wi-Fi by default, keep a saved queue, and support cancellation and retries.
- Replace Android's layered launcher icon with the complete colour image to address the white icon reported on Fold8. This still needs confirmation on that phone.
- Remove the stats shortcut beside Android Home's filters. Your stats remain available in the profile/settings area.

Includes the latest crash fixes from 1.0.5.

The Android APK is attached. The iPhone IPA will be attached by the release workflow; SideStore updates when that build finishes.

The mapping text file helps decode Android crash reports. You do not need it to install the app.

- Fixes the app icon showing as a blank white square on Samsung phones

Includes everything from 1.0.4 (the crash-on-launch fix and built-in crash reports).

- **Fixes the app crashing every time it opens** once your music library loads (anything over a few dozen songs could trigger it)
- If Spitify ever crashes again, the next launch shows a "Send crash report" button, so it can be fixed quickly
- Settings › Help › Send problem report

`Spitify-1.0.4-mapping.txt` is for decoding crash reports; you don't need to download it.

Includes everything from 1.0.3.

- Profile pictures (and custom album art) are no longer sideways
- Fixed the app crashing right after setup when choosing a photo taken with the phone's camera (high-resolution photos ran it out of memory)

Includes everything from 1.0.2.

Fixes 1.0.1 closing itself / "Spitify is crashing frequently" after swiping it away from Recents. Swiping away still stops the music; reopening picks up where you left off.

Includes everything from 1.0.1.

- Swiping Spitify away from Recents now stops the music (Android)
- Daily Mix filler removed; a calmer, less cluttered Home
- Rows never show half-cut artwork or text
- Smoother transitions between the two halves of the Fold8 split view
- Portrait: tap the mini player to open the full player
- Lyrics are fetched automatically when you're online (no more "Search lyrics")

The iPhone IPA is attached automatically by CI once it finishes building; SideStore picks the update up from the source.
First release.
